findings.claim: Goniatites are taught as having "pointed saddles and rounded lobes" (repeated in the collapsible, in practice question 1 option A, in the compare mark scheme, in the match knowledge check and in a flashcard).
findings.truth: The lesson's own ceratite description says saddles are rounded and smooth while the lobes are frilled, and practice option B repeats it. Both cannot be true: the saddles cannot be pointed in a goniatite and rounded in the ceratite that evolved from it by subdividing the lobes. Standard palaeontological usage gives the goniatite rounded saddles and pointed (V-shaped) lobes, but Wikipedia is itself inconsistent here (Ammonoidea: ceratitic sutures have subdivided lobes and rounded undivided saddles; the Goniatites genus page calls the first lateral saddle subangular to angular). The claim that survives every source, and the one the spec actually needs, is the level of frilling: a goniatite suture is a simple zigzag with no frilling on either element. Edits replace the contested saddle/lobe attribution with that.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Ammonoidea (suture types); Wikipedia Goniatitida ("smooth saddles and lobes"); spec 2.3c requires only that the named fossils are told apart by suture line

findings.claim: "A many-stiped (multiramous) form — such as Didymograptus with two stipes pointing downward — is characteristic of the Ordovician."
findings.truth: Didymograptus has two stipes, not many; the sentence contradicts itself. Two-stiped (biramous) forms with pendent stipes are the Ordovician marker; single-stiped forms come later, in the Silurian.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Didymograptus (two rows of cups, Middle to Late Ordovician)

findings.claim: "Examiners regularly find that students give a numerical age ... when asked to state a relative age." and "This single mistake is one of the most frequent errors in exam papers for this topic."
findings.truth: No examiner report or published data supports either claim. The teaching point (relative age must use relational language) is correct and is kept; the invented examiner evidence is removed.

findings.claim: "A single description without a comparison earns no more than half marks."
findings.truth: An invented mark-scheme rule. The real point is that a compare question is not answered by describing one fossil.
findings.evidence: no source; spec gives no such rule

findings.claim: "Examiners frequently award a mark specifically for correct units (Ma or Ga, not just a number)"; the exam tip repeats it; the calculation mark scheme adds "Units must be stated for the second mark."
findings.truth: Three invented mark allocations. Units are required for a complete answer, but no published mark scheme is quoted or known to award a mark for units alone.

findings.claim: "examiners want you to link each scientist to their method AND to the key strength or weakness of that method"
findings.truth: A fabricated statement of examiner intent. The advice itself is sound and is kept in the second person.

findings.claim: "salt is also removed from the ocean by evaporation and the formation of evaporite deposits"
findings.truth: Evaporation removes water and concentrates the remaining salt. Salt leaves the ocean when evaporite minerals precipitate, not by evaporation itself.

findings.claim: "reptiles dominated by the Carboniferous and Permian"
findings.truth: Reptiles first appear in the Carboniferous (Hylonomus, about 312 Ma) but amphibians dominate that period. Reptiles become the dominant land vertebrates in the Permian. The lesson's own Key Fact treats the Carboniferous as first appearance, so the prose also contradicts it.
findings.evidence: spec 2.5b sequence of first appearances; standard vertebrate record

findings.claim: Key Fact lists fish, amphibians, reptiles, mammals, birds and then says "Each group evolved from its predecessor as adaptations to new environments appeared."
findings.truth: Read against that list this makes birds evolve from mammals. Mammals and birds both descend from separate reptile lineages, and the lesson body already says so.
findings.evidence: spec 2.5b/2.5d (Archaeopteryx links non-avian dinosaurs and birds); lesson content_html n7

findings.claim: The mark scheme gives the Chicxulub crater as "approximately 180 km in diameter" while the lesson body teaches "approximately 200 km in diameter".
findings.truth: Published estimates run from about 180 km to about 200 km; Wikipedia now states 200 km. A student who learns the lesson figure would be marked against a key that names a different one, so the key is widened to 180-200 km.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Chicxulub crater ("estimated to be two hundred kilometers in diameter")

findings.claim: Question 5 (a half-life calculation from a 1:3 parent:daughter ratio) is labelled "4 marks - Sequence Geological Events".
findings.truth: It is a maths calculation, not a sequencing task. The label misdescribes what the student has to do.
findings.evidence: the question text itself; the other four-mark labels in this unit

findings.claim: "Hutton first recognised the significance of unconformities at Siccar Point in Scotland in 1788"
findings.truth: Hutton had already found and interpreted unconformities on Arran and at Jedburgh in 1787. Siccar Point (1788) is the most famous, not the first. No mark rides on it.

findings.claim: "They lived during the Devonian and Carboniferous periods" (goniatites)
findings.truth: Goniatites range from the Middle Devonian to the end of the Permian. The Devonian-Carboniferous range is the standard zone-fossil usage taught at GCSE, so no mark is at risk, but the flat claim about their lifespan is not the full range.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Goniatitida (Middle Devonian to Late Permian)

findings.claim: "Confusing these is one of the most common mistakes in the exam" (Key Fact) and "Confusing their suture patterns is one of the most common exam mistakes" (conclusion); lesson 5 has "Examiners sometimes ask students to explain why the absence of a fossil ..."
findings.truth: Unevidenced claims about exam performance. They are not attributed to a mark scheme and do not assert a mark allocation, so they are not edited, but they should go in any future style sweep.

findings.claim: Calendar-year analogy: "the first multicellular animals in late November, the first fish in late November, the first land plants in December"
findings.truth: On a 4,600 Ma to 365-day scale, first multicellular animals (about 600 Ma) fall around 13 November, first fish (about 480 Ma) around 23 November and first land plants (470-425 Ma) in the last week of November. Giving two events the same slot flattens the order the spec asks students to know. The text already flags the analogy as approximate.

findings.claim: The Phanerozoic and the Cambrian base are given as 541 Ma (content, glossary and flashcard); the Palaeozoic as 541-252 Ma.
findings.truth: The current ICS value is 538.8 Ma. 541 Ma is the pre-2022 official figure and is still the value printed in most GCSE textbooks, so no mark is at risk. Change only if the whole subject is re-based on the current chart.

findings.claim: "Holmes also recognised that meteorites ... could be dated radiometrically ... Meteorite dating, combined with the dating of lunar rocks brought back by the Apollo missions, converged on an age of approximately 4,600 million years"
findings.truth: The meteorite lead-isotope age of about 4,550 Ma is Clair Patterson's (1956), and the Apollo samples confirmed rather than established it. The spec's named list stops at Holmes, so the lesson stays in scope, but the credit is loose.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Age of the Earth / Clair Cameron Patterson

findings.claim: "A mineral sample contains equal amounts of potassium-40 and argon-40 ... one half-life has passed"
findings.truth: K-40 decays by branching: about 11 per cent to Ar-40 and about 89 per cent to Ca-40, so an equal K-40 to Ar-40 count is not exactly one half-life. Spec 2.3d asks only for "unstable parent, stable daughter" analysis, so the simplification is the intended GCSE treatment.

summary: No exam-structure, tier or board-naming errors: nothing in the five lessons names Eduqas or WJEC, claims tiers or SPaG, or asserts a component structure, and no banned string appears. The real yield is a reversed-looking goniatite suture description carried through six fields, Didymograptus called many-stiped, six fabricated examiner or mark-scheme claims across four lessons, and three content errors in lessons 4 and 5. All dates, half-lives, decay maths and answer keys recompute correctly.
